body: Is somebody looking into this or should we allow-list those warnings for now? This is creating unnecessary noise in CI.

I'll take a look.

Updates:

1. It looks like 6c0223313bc881847df28e939087df52a833c7c1, which [updates netty to 4.1.85](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/commit/6c0223313bc881847df28e939087df52a833c7c1#diff-2b7d71809e1063e0d0411cbe30d606e12b984790680195567e7b8bde0d078e3fR137), is the commit that introduced the warnings
2. The issue seems to be caused by the netty changes in https://github.com/netty/netty/commit/fe0b5ce16c4508387f999e530a85f2d968e90a3c

So the issue appears to be that with `4.1.85` GraalVM finds the reflection configurations shipped with netty and it tries to load the following classes and register them for reflection:

* `io.netty.handler.codec.compression.Lz4FrameDecoder`
* `io.netty.handler.codec.compression.Lz4FrameEncoder`
* `io.netty.handler.codec.marshalling.CompatibleMarshallingDecoder`
* `io.netty.handler.codec.marshalling.CompatibleMarshallingEncoder`
* `io.netty.handler.codec.marshalling.MarshallingDecoder`
* `io.netty.handler.codec.marshalling.MarshallingEncoder`
* `io.netty.handler.codec.protobuf.ProtobufDecoder`

These classes however reference the following classes that are not on the classpath:

* `net/jpountz/lz4/LZ4Exception`
* `org/jboss/marshalling/ByteInpu`
* `org/jboss/marshalling/ByteOutput`
* `com/google/protobuf/ExtensionRegistryLite`

The solutions I see are the following:

1. Include the necessary dependencies in the classpath.
2. Don't load the reflection configuration from netty (@Sanne I think you are the one who know how to achieve this, do we do it for any other extension?).

I suggest going for 2 since we have had no issues so far with our own configuration, although it might be worth inheriting upstream project configurations at some point.

Unfortunately substitutions are of no help here (since the class loading happens before they are applied and the classes are explicitly loaded).
For `2`, I assume you mean `ExcludeConfigBuildItem` and perhaps `RemovedResourceBuildItem`?

Yes I'd agree with using `ExcludeConfigBuildItem` ; @zakkak see an example here: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/23f43c3d3be6f479f86f697888856a8c65d8136d/extensions/jdbc/jdbc-oracle/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/jdbc/oracle/deployment/OracleMetadataOverrides.java#L110-L117

 needs a bit of fiddling with Regexp :/ And careful, I had to iterate on the current regex as the regex needs to be passed as command line, not all symbols are valid on Windows so it's a bit tricky.

For my sanity I even used unit tests on the constants to be used:

https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/23f43c3d3be6f479f86f697888856a8c65d8136d/extensions/jdbc/jdbc-oracle/deployment/src/test/java/io/quarkus/jdbc/oracle/deployment/RegexMatchTest.java#L18

issue.title: Exclude Netty's reflection configuration files
issue.body:
These are causing warnigns during native image compilation as they try to access classes that are not on the
classpath (e.g. `net.jpountz.lz4.LZ4Exception`).

Closes #29413
